references.text: The same instructions regarding offering the fat and the fat tail from the peace offering, describing which parts of the animal are to be burned on the altar.
Parallel text about the fat tail and the fat covering the entrails in connection with peace offerings from small livestock.
Describes the same pattern for removing fat from the entrails in the sin offering, using the same terminology regarding the fat that covers the entrails.
Prohibition against eating fat from an ox, sheep, or goat, emphasizing that the fat belongs to the Lord.
The same principle of burning the fat covering the entrails on the altar, here in the context of the consecration offering.
Moses takes the fat tail and all the fat on the entrails during the consecration of Aaron and his sons, the same components mentioned in 7:3.
